This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via invalid_value (literal, a string literal in assertAnonymousWriteCarriesNoFile))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via invalid_value (literal, a string literal in assertAnonymousWriteCarriesNoFile))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 431f065177de0cfc9d682b3b18692132390e0c57` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e435c5f6858bc52277571b5cdebf3b4f6639b161` — the merge of head `8102869e46411275625bde02165a6f23adb74ed4` into base `431f065177de0cfc9d682b3b18692132390e0c57`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e435c5f6858bc52277571b5cdebf3b4f6639b161 && git checkout e435c5f6858bc52277571b5cdebf3b4f6639b161
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 431f065177de0cfc9d682b3b18692132390e0c57 8102869e46411275625bde02165a6f23adb74ed4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 431f065177de0cfc9d682b3b18692132390e0c57 && git merge --no-ff 8102869e46411275625bde02165a6f23adb74ed4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 431f065177de0cfc9d682b3b18692132390e0c57
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 431f065177de0cfc9d682b3b18692132390e0c57` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b2f90ab2b51dfdf731c496a2bb6f0702ff98024e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-lifecycle.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-lifecycle.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-read-verdict.integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/backfill-sys-file-public-scope.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/sys-file-copy-backfill-organization-stamping.test.ts + .changeset/25694-anonymous-write-carries-no-file.md, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`buildSession`, the `beforeInsert` / `beforeUpdate` dispatch sites incl. `insertMany` per row), packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts (`callerContext`), packages/core/src/utils/required-emptiness.ts (`isEmptyForRequired`), packages/types/src/validation-failure.ts, packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts (`resolveThrownHttpError`), packages/runtime/src/endpoint-executor.ts, packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts (the class-1 judgement from #25682), packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts (`assembleExecutionContextOrGuest`), packages/core/src/security/anonymous-deny.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts (`resolveRunDataContext`), packages/services/service-storage/src/backfill-file-references.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/backfill-sys-file-public-scope.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/metadata-store.ts, docs/adr/0138 (D2, D9), docs/adr/0112, docs/adr/0114

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept-set change (narrowing only).** The one behavioural edit is a module-private predicate run first in both before-write hooks the storage lifecycle already registers (`beforeInsert`, `beforeUpdate`), ahead of the #7102 predicate refusal and ahead of copy-on-claim. A record write is refused when, and only when, all of: the object declares at least one `FILE_REFERENCE_TYPES` field and `sys_file` is registered (`activeFileFields`); the write has a caller (`referencingCallerOf`: a hook session exists and is not `isSystem`); that caller carries no `userId`; and the payload sets a file field to a value that `isEmptyForRequired` does not call empty. Everything else reaches the driver exactly as on `main`:

- a signed-in caller (every transport-assembled human or agent principal carries `userId`; `anonymous-deny.ts` already 401s a user-less, non-system request in every domain outside ADR-0138 D2 classes 4 and 5) — unchanged, pinned by the unit and integration controls;
- a system write (`isSystem`, incl. a `runAs: 'system'` flow, engine self-writes, the in-repo backfills, which write under `SYSTEM_CTX`, and the CLI migrations) — `referencingCallerOf` returns `null` before the predicate looks at anything;
- a context-less programmatic write (a bare kernel, a seed, a provenance-only `{ flowRunId }` context) — `buildSession` returns `undefined` for a context with nothing session-worthy, so `!ctx.session` holds and the write is not judged;
- a user-less write that omits every file field, sets one to `null` / `''` / `[]` on a multi-valued field, or clears a file field on update — passes (`isEmptyForRequired`), pinned by the controls, so an anonymous update may still leave or clear a file field under a deployment's guest grants;
- an object with no file field — exits before the predicate (pinned).

Non-system flow data nodes cannot present a user-less context either: `resolveRunDataContext` yields `isSystem: true` for `runAs: 'system'` and otherwise the triggering user's `userId`, or throws `UnscopedRunDataAccessError`. So ADR-0138 D2 class 5 reaches this hook only as system or as a user, and the dev's "closed by construction" reading holds in the code read.

**Placement is correct and complete for D2's write classes.** Every engine write path dispatches the before hooks: single insert, `insertMany` (per row), by-id update and the unscoped predicate update (`dispatchUnscopedMultiWriteHooks`, where the new predicate runs before the #7102 bulk refusal, as the hunk's comment says). The class-4 door (`authRequired: false` object operations, the D9 guest envelope with no `userId`) therefore cannot reach the driver with a file value through any write verb, and a door added later inherits the rule without a per-door edit. Class 1 keeps its own door-side judgement from #25682, and now has the engine rule beneath it; classes 2, 3 and 6 are reads. Guarding at the storage lifecycle rather than in `packages/rest` / `packages/runtime` is the right altitude for a rule about the file-reference claim path, and it sits inside the claim's file surface.

**Envelope (ADR-0112 / ADR-0114).** The refusal is `validationFailure(...)` from `@objectstack/types`: `name: 'ValidationError'`, `code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED'` (a ledger member), `fields[]` with one entry per refused field carrying the closed ADR-0114 catalog code `invalid_value`, the field's label (or its name when none is declared) and a message. The status is supplied at the boundary: `resolveThrownHttpError` maps a `ValidationError` with no declared status to 400 and passes `fields[]` through, and `endpoint-executor.ts` (the class-4 door) states it uses that same table. The same constructor, emptiness rule and field code the class-1 door uses, so the two doors answer alike. No new error code, no new status, no new catalog key, no new i18n key. The refusal is thrown before any `sys_file` lookup, before the read verdict is asked and before any bytes move; the unit pins assert `authorizeRead` and `storage.download` are not called and no `sys_file` write occurs, the integration pins assert no record row and an unchanged `sys_file` table on a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver`.

**Public surface.** `assertAnonymousWriteCarriesNoFile` is module-private; `installFileReferenceHooks`'s signature is unchanged; no export is added or removed. The two new imports (`isEmptyForRequired` from `@objectstack/core`, `validationFailure` from `@objectstack/types`) are both already declared `dependencies` of `@objectstack/service-storage` and already imported elsewhere in the package, so no manifest or dependency-graph change.

**Tests.** 11 unit cases (6 refusal: four value shapes on insert, update, several fields in one envelope; 5 controls) and 7 integration cases (5 refusal across the file arms the #25692 read verdict distinguishes, incl. an unowned `public_read` file and a value naming no platform file; 2 controls). Each refusal asserts `code` and the `fields[]` entry; the one thing the committed tests do not assert is the HTTP status, which is a boundary property the cited resolver supplies (judged above from the code). The dev's red-first commits and ablation are reported, not re-run here.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/service-storage`, `fix(storage)!:` header, the BREAKING section with Before / Now / Fix, and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` + `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial on both carriers (PR body and changeset). The level follows the convention for a runtime refusal with no protocol move: `none` takes `patch`; a narrowing keeps its BREAKING banner. The ADR-0087 disposition is exactly one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, and its argument is correct on the facts: no spec key, authorable spelling, stored row or shape moves and nothing exported is removed or narrowed, so there is nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite; the remedy is a change of who provides the file. The Check Changeset and the PM dispatch-gates lint check-runs on this head are green.

Disclosure: the changeset and PR body describe the rule and the door class in ADR-0138 D2's own public vocabulary (a caller with no user may no longer put a value in a file field; which class the change closes). Neither carries a request shape, an object, a step sequence or a pre-fix outcome, so the disclosure discipline holds on both carriers.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Declared departure (lifecycle guard, no door edit in rest/runtime): endorsed.** One guard on the hook every engine write dispatches closes the class, including a door declared later; a per-door edit would have left the rule to be re-derived at each one. The residual it leaves is stated in the PR body and is real but narrow: the hooks are installed only where the storage service is composed, and `activeFileFields` exits when `sys_file` is not registered, so a kernel composed without the storage service does not apply ruling C to a non-platform value (an external URL) in a file field. `serve` always mounts the storage service; noted, not a defect of this card.
- **"No user" is read off the caller, not off `principalKind: 'guest'`.** The rule is therefore slightly wider than the D9 guest envelope: a non-system context that carries an organization and no user is judged anonymous too. In the repo the only writers presenting that shape target `sys_file` (`metadata-store.ts`, excluded by `activeFileFields`) or settings objects with no file field, so nothing in-repo is caught. The wider reading is the conservative direction and matches the caller the #25692 read verdict is asked about; flagged so the seat knows the boundary is "no user", not "the guest envelope".
- **The two edited fixtures** (`sys-file-copy-backfill-organization-stamping.test.ts`, three cases; `backfill-sys-file-public-scope.test.ts`, one helper) drove a copy-on-claim record write with a hook session or context carrying an organization and no user, purely as fixture setup for a different subject (organization stamping and scope on the copy). That shape is the anonymous case under the new rule, so they now name a user; the backfills themselves write under `SYSTEM_CTX` and are not judged. No platform path was caught: this is a test-only caller shape, and the assertions are unchanged.
- **Dev flags / open_questions:** `open_questions` is empty. The dev's one out-of-scope finding, the dogfood `authz-probe-blind-spot.test.ts` red (the `handleI18nRequest` control count in `packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts`), is reported as red on `main` independently of this diff and neither file is touched here: out of scope for this card, left with the seat.
- **Check-runs on the head at review time (44):** none failed; 13 were still `in_progress` (Test Core 1-8, Build Core, Type Check workspace and consumer gates, Lint CI/release/engine gates, Lint scoped slot lookup and corpus). Everything concluded is `success` or `skipped` (UI, docs, opt-in and sharded dogfood jobs skipped by the path filter; the whole-PR Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR size, claim and single-writer guards all green). This verdict is on the diff; the merge group's own guard reads convergence.
- Not in scope and not touched: `packages/spec/**`, any governed path, the class-1 door, the class-4 door in `@objectstack/runtime`.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-0k5uer`
Reviewed-by: `session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo`

**VERDICT: PASS**
